svg.title: A Truly Global War: Mobilising the British Empire & Forgotten Fronts (1914–1918)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 9 1:50m global GIS historical atlas map spanning the Caribbean, Great Britain and the Western Front, Africa, the Ottoman Middle East and Gallipoli, undivided British India, Shandong (China), Australia, and New Zealand, charting over 4 million colonial and Dominion soldiers, carriers, and labourers alongside Allied maritime supply lifelines.

text.tspan: Largest volunteer army; Khudadad Khan VC (1914)
ANZAC, British, Irish & Indian troops fight Ottomans
Troops & porters in bush; >100,000 carrier deaths
~140k Chinese workers dig trenches & unload shells

g.text: >4 million colonial & Dominion soldiers and workers
Empire Troop, Wheat, Wool & Oil Sea-Lanes
Chinese Labour Corps & African Sea Transfers

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 9 ENQUIRY: THE GREAT WAR (1914–1918)
A Truly Global War: Mobilising the British Empire & Forgotten Fronts (1914–18)
Britain’s war effort relied on over 4 million colonial & Dominion troops and labourers plus global wheat, wool and oil lifelines across five continents.
From Khudadad Khan VC at Ypres to ANZACs, Caribbean BWIR, African Carriers & Chinese labourers, imperial sacrifice won the war yet faced post-1918 erasure.
